title: ALMA detection of a disc-dominated [C II] emission line at z=4.6 in the luminous QSO J1554+1937
question: What is the origin (rotating disc vs bulge) of the broad [C II] line in the luminous z=4.6 QSO J1554+1937, and how does this affect its position relative to the local M-sigma relation?

what.value: Bolometric luminosity and target selection from QSO catalog

evidence.quote: We first identified luminous QSOs as potential targets from the multi-wavelength QSO catalog of (cite: krawczyk13)

what.value: SMBH mass (2.8±0.5)e10 Msun from C IV width

evidence.loc: 4.6 Measuring the central black hole mass
evidence.quote: (cite: shenEtal11) estimated the SMBH in J1554+1937 to have a mass of $M_\mathrm{BH} = (2.8\pm0.5)\times10^{10}~M_\odot$.
We therefore use the linear relation from (cite: pizzella05) to represent the relationship between $\sigma$ and $v_0$.
we are now equipped to compare J1554+1937 to the local $M$–$\sigma$ relation (cite: kormendyHo_review)

recipe.method: Run NAASC scripts in CASA 4.2, clean with Briggs weighting, one round of phase-only self-calibration

recipe.goal: Measure continuum and line sizes and fluxes
recipe.method: Gaussian fit in the uv-plane with uvmodelfit for continuum and line; moment 0, 1, 2 maps
key_parameters: moment 0 over 337.3-338.2 GHz; moment 1 pixels with S/N ≥4 of ~2 mJy rms

recipe.method: Idealised disc with v(r)=v0[1-exp(-r/r0)], exponential surface brightness, Gaussian dispersion, inclination, integrated over disc
Mdyn/Msun ≈1.16e5 v0^2 D with v0 sin i from half-width at 20% of maximum
assumptions: rotating disc; D=1.6 kpc (line) or 2.0 kpc (continuum)

recipe.goal: Bulge velocity dispersion from disc rotation
recipe.method: Pizzella et al. linear v0-sigma relation, then aperture correction to r_e/2
Place the source relative to the Kormendy & Ho relation with SMBH mass from Shen et al. for various inclinations

evidence.quote: The actual redshift of the line is approximately 4.627
The integrated flux density resulting from the fit is $12.70\pm0.12$ mJy at $\sim344$ GHz.
The integrated flux density is to be $9.40\pm0.40$ Jy km s$^{-1}$
corresponding to a line luminosity of $5.9\times10^9~\mathrm{L}_\odot$

answer_key.quantity: Dynamical mass x sin^2 i (continuum size)

not_stated_but_needed: Channel width and cell/image size used in clean
Line-free channels used for continuum subtraction and continuum map
How the moment maps and 20 per cent half-width were measured (visual)
Details of the line profile model fitting/inclination integration
Number of execution blocks and observing date
missing_for_reproduction: Exact moment map thresholds and line-width measurement
score_reason: Short single dataset with public ALMA data and simple recipe, but several imaging details and visual measurements are unspecified.
rediscovery_reason: Single archival dataset, numeric results (flux, FWHM, sizes) are recoverable with standard CASA steps.
